questions.title: Practising Swings in Thick Grass – Changing the Grass Behind Your Ball
questions.question: Your ball is sitting in thick, long grass. Before you hit your shot, you make a practice swing and push down some of the grass right behind your ball. This makes your next shot easier. What happens?

choices.text: There is no penalty because you were just practising.
There is no penalty because the ball did not move.
You get the general penalty because you changed the grass behind your ball to make your shot easier.

questions.explanation: You can make practice swings, but you cannot push down the grass or change anything around your ball to make your shot easier. If you do, you get the general penalty. This is because you are not allowed to improve the grass, sand or ground behind your ball before you play.

vocabulary.simpleMeaning: This means you lose two shots (strokes) in stroke play or lose the hole in match play.
This means the grass, sand, ground, or anything that can change the way you hit the ball.

questions.teachingTip: When practising your swing, be careful not to touch or move the grass or ground right near your ball.
likelyMisconceptions: Some kids think if the ball does not move, there is no problem.
Some kids think practise swings do not count.

questions.title: Practice Swing in Long Rough – Improving Conditions Affecting the Stroke
questions.question: Your ball is lying in long rough. Before playing your shot, you take a practice swing that knocks down some of the long grass directly behind the ball, making your next swing easier. What is the correct ruling?

choices.text: There is no penalty because it was only a practice swing.
There is no penalty because you did not move the ball.
You receive the general penalty because you improved the conditions affecting your stroke.

questions.explanation: You are allowed to take practice swings, but you must not improve the conditions affecting your stroke. If your practice swing deliberately or accidentally knocks down long grass directly behind the ball, improving your next swing, you receive the general penalty for improving the conditions affecting your stroke. See Rule 8.1a.
